reference_sql:
SELECT s.city, SUM(l.quantity * l.unit_price_eur - l.line_discount_eur) AS revenue_eur
FROM order_lines l
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.city
alternatives: SELECT st.city, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM sales s JOIN stores st ON st.store_code = s.store_code WHERE s.order_month = DATE '2025-03-01' GROUP BY st.city

SELECT s.city, SUM(l.quantity * l.unit_price_eur) - SUM(l.line_discount_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM stores s JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id WHERE CAST(o.order_ts AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2025-03-01' AND DATE '2025-03-31' GROUP BY s.city

other_way.sql: SELECT st.city, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue_eur FROM sales s JOIN stores st ON st.store_code = s.store_code WHERE s.order_month = DATE '2025-03-01' GROUP BY st.city
other_way.tradeoff: Starting from sales and joining only stores is shorter, but it works only because sales already holds net revenue.
